title: Republic of Baden
capsule: The revolutionary Republic of Baden emerged in May 1849 when radical democrats and mutinous army units expelled Grand Duke Leopold and proclaimed a republic during the final convulsion of the German revolutions of 1848–49, with Lorenz Brentano heading a provisional government. The uprising attracted foreign volunteers—including Poles, Hungarians, and Friedrich Engels—and briefly controlled most of the Grand Duchy's territory. Prussian troops under Crown Prince Wilhelm crossed the Rhine in June 1849, routed the republican forces at Waghäusel (21 June) and at Rastatt (23 July), and reinstated the grand ducal government; the last resistance ended in late July 1849, and the Wikidata end date of 1853 likely reflects the delayed formal restoration of the Baden constitution under Prussian occupation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Republic of Baden controlled the territory of the existing Grand Duchy during its two-month existence in 1849; its borders are identical to those of the pre-existing grand duchy and are cartographically well established.
